title: Shepherds in the Dark Fields
paragraphs: Outside the town, on the cold hillsides, shepherds were watching their sheep through the night. They were ordinary working people, up in the dark, doing a job that smelled of wool and wet grass. Suddenly the sky lit up and an angel stood before them. They were terrified. "Fear not," said the angel (KJV). He brought good news of great joy for everyone: that today in David's town a Saviour had been born, and they would find the baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger. The first people to hear were not kings or priests. They were the ones nobody asked. And God sent the news to them first.
wonder: I wonder why God chose to tell the shepherds first?
activity: Make a sheep from cotton wool, and add a small gold thread collar.
prayer: God of the ordinary and the overlooked, thank you for sending good news to everyone. Amen.
alt: Shepherds and sheep on a dark hillside look up at a burst of golden light in the night sky.
hidden: A small lamb lifting its head to look at the light.
translation: Retold in our own words, with a short quotation from the King James Version.
